articleBody:
Wondering if your website is geared up for the new world of AI search and answer engines? It's not just about content anymore; technical readiness plays a huge role. Here's a practical checklist to guide you.

- [ ] Check `robots.txt` and `meta robots` — Ensure these aren't accidentally blocking Googlebot, OAI-SearchBot, or other relevant AI crawlers from important pages. If they can't crawl it, they can't cite it.
- [ ] Verify page indexability and crawl status — Use tools like Google Search Console to confirm your key pages are indexed and free of crawl errors. No index, no AI mention.
- [ ] Inspect mobile performance and structure — AI systems value user experience, and a fast, well-structured mobile site signals quality and readability.
- [ ] Review structured data for accuracy — Make sure any JSON-LD schema (like FAQPage or Article) precisely matches the visible content on your page; don't just add it for show.
- [ ] Assess content for clarity and fact density — Your answers should be direct, evidence-based, current, and easy for an AI to extract. Vague content gets overlooked.
- [ ] Confirm consistency of business information — Ensure your Name, Address, Phone (NAP) and other business details are uniform across your site. Inconsistencies confuse AI.
- [ ] Test JavaScript rendering — If key content is hidden behind JavaScript that crawlers can't execute, it's invisible to AI. Use developer tools to check this.
- [ ] Look for thin or outdated FAQ content — AI loves detailed, current answers. Sparse or old FAQs won't cut it.

How to use this checklist: Go through each item methodically. If you find issues, prioritize fixing the most critical ones first, like blocking crawlers or fundamental indexability problems. This isn't a one-time check; regular reviews keep your site AI-ready. If tackling these technical elements feels overwhelming, especially with a large or complex site, that’s a clear sign to bring in a professional.
